stem: At the start of an AI engagement a client says, "We want a chatbot." Which discovery question is the most useful first step?

options.text: Which large language model would you like us to use?
Which task or decision is slow, costly or error-prone today, who does it, and how would we know it had improved?
How many users will have the chatbot on their phone?
Do you already have an API key for a model provider?

explanation: Discovery starts from the business problem and a measurable outcome. Model choice, channel and credentials are solution details that depend on the answer. Without a baseline you cannot tell whether an AI solution helped.

stem: Which of these is a testable non-functional requirement for an internal policy-answering assistant?

options.text: The assistant should feel fast and trustworthy.
For at least 95% of questions the first answer token appears within 3 seconds and every answer cites at least one source document.
The assistant will use the best available model.
The assistant must be user friendly.

explanation: A testable requirement has a measurable threshold and a way to check it. "Fast", "best" and "user friendly" cannot be verified, so they cannot be accepted or rejected.

stem: A head of HR asks for "an AI chatbot for HR". You have two weeks for discovery. HR data includes health and pay information, and the employee base spans several countries.
constraints: Stakeholders include HR, Legal and IT security

options.text: Run workshops to rank the top HR task types by volume and pain, map the data sources and owners for each, and record data-protection and approval constraints before any tool or model is chosen.
Build a prototype over all HR documents to find out what is possible.
Select a vendor so that procurement can start in parallel.
Send a questionnaire asking employees what they want from a chatbot and design from the answers.

rationales.text: Scope, data sensitivity and success measures decide the architecture, so they must be known first.
A prototype is cheap, so doing it first removes the need for discovery.
Different task types (policy lookup, personal records, case handling) have very different risk profiles and need different designs.
Vendor selection is the main architectural decision.

explanation: Discovery should convert a vague wish into prioritised use cases with owners, data sources, risks and success measures. A prototype over unscoped sensitive data is itself a risk, and picking a vendor first inverts the decision order.
model_answer: Rank use cases by volume, pain and risk; separate public policy lookup from personal-data tasks; identify data owners and legal constraints per jurisdiction; agree measurable success criteria; then choose approach and tooling. A bounded prototype on non-sensitive policy documents may follow to test feasibility.

rubric.criterion: Starts from use cases and outcomes, not tools

stem: Sales wants an assistant to send customer email replies automatically. Legal wants a human to review every reply. Both are senior stakeholders and each says the other is blocking value.
constraints: Replies range from order status to complaints and contract queries
Brand and regulatory exposure for some categories

options.text: Turn the conflict into an explicit decision: classify reply categories by risk, propose auto-send only for low-risk templated categories and approval for the rest, record the rule as a requirement with acceptance criteria, and ask both stakeholders to sign it.
Side with Sales because volume is the problem and add review later if complaints appear.
Require review of every reply because Legal carries the risk.
Escalate to the sponsor and wait for a ruling before doing any design work.

rationales.text: Risk differs by message type, so a single rule for all replies is unlikely to be right.
The loudest stakeholder should win to keep the project moving.
Making the policy an explicit, signed requirement stops it being reopened implicitly later.
The conflict is a political matter that architecture cannot help with.

explanation: Conflicting requirements are resolved by making the trade-off explicit and tying it to risk tiers. Both extremes either ignore real exposure or discard the value case.
model_answer: Categorise replies by risk and reversibility, define the automation boundary per category, add human-in-the-loop for higher-risk ones, write the rule with measurable acceptance criteria (for example the share of auto-sent replies that required correction), and record the decision and sign-off.

rubric.criterion: Recognises the conflict as a trade-off to design for
Records the decision and gets agreement
Keeps value from automation where risk is low
